scenario.title: 研討會、業界活動上的交流
scenario.context: 在業界活動上，除了 small talk 還要能表達驚訝和強調：「我從來沒看過這麼棒的展」「她不但是設計師，還是作家」。英文用倒裝句（Never have I…、Not only… but also…）讓語氣更有份量，演講和簡報尤其常用。

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.en: Hi, mind if I sit here? These conference chairs are brutal.
lines.zh: 嗨，介意我坐這嗎？這些研討會的椅子好難坐。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Ha, go ahead. That's one way to break the ice.
lines.zh: 哈，請坐。這也是一種破冰的方式。

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.en: I'm Ben. I run a small branding studio in Taichung.
lines.zh: 我是 Ben，在台中經營一間小型品牌工作室。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Minz. I'm a freelance illustrator. Wait, did you work at Blue Door Agency?
lines.zh: 我是 Minz，自由插畫家。等等，你是不是在藍門廣告待過？

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.en: I did! Small world. We must have overlapped.
lines.zh: 對！世界真小，我們一定有重疊過。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Never have I seen such a packed keynote. That speaker was incredible.
lines.zh: 我從來沒看過這麼滿的主題演講。那位講者太厲害了。

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.en: Right? Not only is she a great designer, but she's also a bestselling author.
lines.zh: 對吧？她不只是很棒的設計師，還是暢銷作家。

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.en: Sorry, I promised myself I wouldn't talk shop all day.
lines.zh: 抱歉，我答應自己今天不要一直聊工作。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: It's a design conference. What else would we talk about?
lines.zh: 這是設計研討會，不聊工作聊什麼？

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.en: Fair. At my studio, the water-cooler talk is all about fonts.
lines.zh: 也是。我們工作室茶水間聊的全是字體。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Only rarely do I meet people who get excited about kerning.
lines.zh: 我很少遇到會對字距興奮的人。

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.en: Well, now you've met one. Let's keep in touch.
lines.zh: 嗯，現在你遇到一個了。保持聯絡吧。

patterns.en: What did you think of the keynote?
patterns.zh: 你覺得主題演講怎麼樣？

patterns.en: We must have crossed paths before.
What are you working on these days?
I'd love to hear more about ___.

patterns.zh: 我們在 LinkedIn 上加一下吧。

patterns.en: Enjoy the rest of the conference!
patterns.zh: 祝你接下來的研討會愉快！

chinglish.wrong: Never I have seen such a big crowd.
chinglish.right: Never have I seen such a big crowd. / I've never seen such a big crowd.
chinglish.why: 否定詞放句首時，主詞和助動詞要倒裝。不確定的話，用正常語序 I've never… 最安全。

chinglish.wrong: Not only she is a designer, but also a writer.
chinglish.right: Not only is she a designer, but she's also a writer.
chinglish.why: Not only 放句首要倒裝；後半句也要有完整主詞動詞。

chinglish.right: Nice to meet you. / Great to meet you.
chinglish.why: 「很高興認識你」直翻 know 不自然，初次見面用 meet。

chinglish.wrong: Please give me your name card.
chinglish.right: Could I get your card? / Do you have a card?
chinglish.why: name card 是亞洲英文說法，美式說 business card 或 card。

grammar.title: 倒裝 Not only… / Never have I…
grammar.oneLiner: 否定或限制詞（never、rarely、not only、only then）放句首時，後面要用問句語序（助動詞 + 主詞）。
whenToUse: Never have I + p.p.：Never have I seen such a crowd.
Rarely / Seldom do I + V：Rarely do I meet people like that.
Only + 時間 / 條件 + 助動詞 + 主詞：Only then did I realize…
Not only + 助動詞 + 主詞…, but (主詞) also…：Not only is she talented, but she's also kind.
No sooner had I… than…：一…就…（很正式）。
倒裝語氣正式、有強調效果，常出現在演講、寫作、簡報；日常口語用正常語序就好。
grammar.whyWeGetItWrong: 中文強調時只要把詞移到前面：「從來沒看過這麼多人」，語序不用變。英文把否定詞移到句首後，後面必須變成問句語序，這對台灣人來說非常反直覺，常寫成 Never I have seen。好消息是：日常對話不用倒裝也完全沒問題，但聽得懂、偶爾用在簡報裡，會讓你的英文顯得很有程度。

examples.correct: Never have I been so nervous.
examples.incorrect: Never I have been so nervous.
examples.note: 助動詞 have 放主詞前。

examples.correct: Not only did we finish early, but we also came in under budget.
examples.note: 過去式用 did 倒裝。

examples.correct: Rarely do you find a client this easy to work with.
Only after the meeting did I understand the problem.

examples.note: 日常口語用正常語序即可。

quiz.question: Not only ___ talented, but she's also generous.
quiz.explanation: Not only + 助動詞 + 主詞。

quiz.question: Rarely ___ I get a chance to meet my heroes. (助動詞)
Only then ___ how important the project was.
quiz.explanation: Only then + did + 主詞 + V。

quiz.question: Which is the most natural in casual conversation?
options: Never have I eaten such good food.
I've never eaten such good food.
Never I have eaten such good food.
quiz.explanation: 日常口語用正常語序最自然；倒裝較正式。

slang.usage: 在陌生場合開啟對話、緩和氣氛。icebreaker = 破冰活動。

examples.en: A joke about the weather is a classic way to break the ice.
examples.zh: 聊天氣的笑話是經典的破冰方式。

examples.en: We started the workshop with an icebreaker.
examples.zh: 工作坊一開始先做了破冰活動。

slang.usage: 發現彼此有共同認識的人或經歷時說。It's a small world!

examples.en: You know my cousin? Small world!
examples.zh: 你認識我表哥？世界真小！

examples.en: The design industry in Taiwan is a small world.

slang.usage: 在非工作場合聊工作的事，常帶點「又在聊工作了」的自嘲。

examples.en: No talking shop at dinner, please!
Whenever designers get together, we end up talking shop.
examples.zh: 設計師聚在一起最後都會聊工作。

slang.usage: 同事在茶水間、飲水機旁的非正式聊天。

examples.en: Remote work means less water-cooler talk.
examples.zh: 遠端工作代表茶水間閒聊變少了。

examples.en: The finale was the only water-cooler talk this week.
examples.zh: 這週茶水間只在聊那部劇的大結局。

review.question: A: I've never been to a conference this big. B: ___
review.explanation: 複習第 80 單元：否定附和用 neither。

review.question: By the time the keynote started, every seat ___.
review.explanation: 複習第 79 單元：by the time + 過去完成（被動）。

review.question: Feel ___ to grab a coffee before the next talk.
review.explanation: 複習第 77 單元：feel free to。

review.question: You ___ try talking to the speaker after the session.
review.explanation: 複習第 73 單元：could 提供選項。

review.question: I came to the conference ___ meet new clients.
I ___ brought more business cards. I ran out.
review.explanation: 複習第 49 單元：should have + p.p.。

review.question: The session starts in two minutes. We ___ go.
